Hyman (Ports) 17:32 3.Herring(B'Hth)/D.Cooke (Port) 17:39

In the Southern Counties A.A.A. 6 miles championship at Portsmouth on April 28th, Bill Kerr finished an excellent 5th in 29:19.4, breaking Charlie Dabb's club record by 8.6 seconds. Winner was Batty (28:55.0) from Strong (28a58.4) and D.

Portsmouth then produced their first trump card----Dave Cooke, It was unfortunate that young Tony Fairclough should meet Cooke at this time, for the Portsmouth man turned an eight second deficit into a 58 second lead and recorded second fastest time of the day.

Ron Linstead took over 31 secs. in arrears and although passing the Poly and making up some ground on the leaders, was forced to give way to David Cooke of Portsmouth, who brought his club into the picture for the first time, only 4 secs. behind T.V.H. and to Surrey A.C. for whom Hazeltine was in good form.
Unfortunately, on Stage 4, Dave Cooke of Pompey got ample revenge for his team by taking 39 seconds off Charlie Walker and giving his twin, John Cooke, a useful lead.

On a flooded, heavy track at Southampton on Sept.4th, and in a constant downpour, Bill Kerr finished off the track season with an excellent 13:57.4 three miles. He was 2nd to Batty (13:47.4) but beat the Portsmouth runners D.
9. · D. Cooke · Portsmouth · 49:23
He also could make no ground on the leaders wh[illegible] were represented by David Cooke and at the end of this stage, with only one lap to go, Portsmouth were over 2½ minutes ahead.

Dave Cooke picked up over a minute on Derby to take his club into 2nd place and to set up a fantastically fast stage record. In the meantime, Brian Kilby had ensured a 2nd successive win for Coventry.
John Moore was the first Belgravian home with 1:30:43 in 18th position. Winner was D.Cooke(Portsmouth)1:24:20.
Mel Thorpe had the difficult job of staying with D. Cooke and was unequal to the task, by 31 seconds.

The fourth stage is a new and crucial leg being one of the longest and Charlie Dabbs tackled it in workmanlike manner with the knowledge that Dave Cooke,one of the Portsmouth twins,was chasing him.Charles ran well to keep out in front although our lead was now cut back to five seconds.

The Bels really had their tails up now and Geoff North collected a 3rd stage record for the North family (Gerry holds two), and thrashed Dave Cooke of Pompy (2nd fastest) by no less than 45seconds, giving Tony Fairclough an invincible lead of 3:22 for the final stage.

Pat Newell was next to run on the first of the short circuits (3½ miles) and soon overtook the Portsmouth runner (Plumpton) but Reading and Windsor were soon upon him and Pat had to be content to hand over to Mel Thorpe in 4th place. Mel underwent a similar experience by passing all three runners ah…
Ahead, however, Dick Taylor of Coventry was building up a good lead by dropping Dave Cooke of Portsmouth,who in turn took his team away from Bristol.
3. · D.Cooke · Portsmouth · 29:51

Portsmouth,through a fast run by Dave Cooke, had now surfaced into 4th position but were still 1:42 down. Fairclough had not for long been back in training, but he rose to the occasion and was the third fastest of our six long stage runners.
